title: AP Precalculus 2.3 — Exponential Functions
question: How do the sign of the coefficient and the base decide whether an exponential function increases or decreases, where it heads at each end, and its intercept, range and asymptote?

questions.title: Increasing or decreasing?
questions.prompt:
Consider:

\[
f(x)=-4\cdot3^x
\]

Which statement is correct?
choices: The function increases and stays positive.
The function decreases and stays positive.
The function increases and stays negative.
The function decreases and stays negative.
questions.solution:
Check successive values:

\[
f(0)=-4,\qquad f(1)=-12,\qquad f(2)=-36
\]

The values become more negative, so the function **decreases**. Because \(3^x>0\), its output is always negative.

questions.title: End behavior
questions.prompt:
Consider:

\[
g(x)=5\left(\frac12\right)^x
\]

What happens to \(g(x)\) at each end of the graph?
questions.solution:
A base between \(0\) and \(1\) produces decay when the coefficient is positive:

\[
g(-3)=40,\qquad g(0)=5,\qquad g(3)=\frac58
\]

Moving right, the curve approaches \(0\) **from above**. Moving left, it grows without bound.

questions.title: Graph features
questions.prompt:
Consider:

\[
h(x)=-2\left(\frac13\right)^x
\]

Which option correctly identifies its **\(y\)-intercept, range, and horizontal asymptote**?
questions.solution:
At \(x=0\):

\[
h(0)=-2\left(\frac13\right)^0=-2
\]

The outputs are always negative and approach—but never reach—\(0\). Therefore:

\[
\boxed{\text{Range: }(-\infty,0),\qquad \text{horizontal asymptote: }y=0}
\]
